title: Comparar y cuantificar
description: Cómo comparar personas y cosas, y cómo hablar de cantidades.
objectives: Usar as ... as y not as ... as
Distinguir sustantivos contables e incontables y usar some y any
Usar much, many, a lot of, a few y a little

subtopics.title: Comparativos
subtopics.goal: Comparar dos cosas con -er o more.
keyPoints: Adjetivos cortos: + -er + than: tall → taller than.
Adjetivos largos: more + adjetivo + than: more expensive than.
Consonante + y → -ier: happy → happier. Consonante-vocal-consonante: big → bigger.
Irregulares: good → better, bad → worse, far → farther / further.

examples.en: My brother is taller than me.
examples.es: Mi hermano es más alto que yo.

examples.en: This phone is more expensive than that one.
examples.es: Este teléfono es más caro que ese.

examples.en: Today's weather is worse than yesterday's.
examples.es: Hoy el clima está peor que ayer.

commonMistakes.wrong: She is more tall than me.
commonMistakes.why: Los adjetivos cortos forman el comparativo con -er.

commonMistakes.wrong: It's better that the other one.
commonMistakes.right: It's better than the other one.
commonMistakes.why: En las comparaciones se usa than, no that.

subtopics.title: Superlativos
subtopics.goal: Decir cuál es el más o el menos de un grupo.
keyPoints: Adjetivos largos: the most + adjetivo: the most interesting.
Irregulares: the best, the worst, the farthest.
Con lugares y grupos se usa in: the best player in the team.

examples.en: It's the biggest city in the country.
examples.es: Es la ciudad más grande del país.

examples.en: This is the most beautiful beach I know.
examples.es: Es la playa más linda que conozco.

examples.en: He's the best student in the class.
examples.es: Es el mejor alumno de la clase.

commonMistakes.why: Big es un adjetivo corto: superlativo con -est y consonante duplicada.

subtopics.title: As ... as y not as ... as
keyPoints: as + adjetivo + as = tan ... como: She's as tall as her mother.
not as + adjetivo + as = no tan ... como: The bus isn't as fast as the train.
El adjetivo va en su forma normal, sin -er ni more.

examples.en: My house is as big as yours.
examples.es: Mi casa es tan grande como la tuya.

examples.en: The movie isn't as good as the book.
examples.es: La película no es tan buena como el libro.

examples.en: It's not as cold as last winter.
examples.es: No hace tanto frío como el invierno pasado.

commonMistakes.why: Con as ... as el adjetivo no lleva -er.

subtopics.title: Contables e incontables: some y any
subtopics.goal: Distinguir contables de incontables y usar some y any.
keyPoints: Contables: se pueden contar (an apple, two apples). Incontables: no tienen plural (water, money, information, advice).
some en afirmativas: I have some friends / some money.
any en negativas y preguntas: I don't have any money. Do you have any questions?
Para ofrecer o pedir se usa some: Would you like some coffee?

examples.en: There's some milk in the fridge.
examples.es: Hay algo de leche en la heladera.

examples.en: Can I have some water, please?
examples.es: ¿Me das un poco de agua, por favor?

commonMistakes.why: Advice es incontable: no lleva a o an ni plural.
Information es incontable y no tiene plural.

subtopics.title: Much, many, a lot of, a few y a little
subtopics.goal: Hablar de cantidades con el cuantificador correcto.
keyPoints: many + contables en plural: many books. much + incontables: much time.
much y many se usan sobre todo en negativas y preguntas; en afirmativas se prefiere a lot of.
a few (unos pocos) + contables; a little (un poco) + incontables.
How many...? y How much...? para preguntar cantidades.

examples.en: How many people were at the party?
I have a few friends in London.

commonMistakes.wrong: How much chairs do we need?
commonMistakes.right: How many chairs do we need?
commonMistakes.why: Chairs es contable: se usa how many.
